_comment: Copy to ~/.config/htpc-remote/devices.json and chmod 600 — it holds secrets.
Override the location with the HTPC_REMOTE_DEVICES environment variable.
Getting the values for a Tuya/Smart Life IR blaster:
1. pip install tinytuya && python -m tinytuya wizard
(needs a free iot.tuya.com cloud project linked to your Smart Life
account; see the wiki page 'TV and IR Control')
2. The wizard writes devices.json — take 'key' as local_key, plus the
hub id and the per-TV remote id it lists.
Transports:
cloud — fires keys from the codeset Smart Life already configured.
No learning needed; adds ~200-500ms and needs internet.
local — replays learned base64 codes over the LAN. Fast and offline,
but OFF by default: many of these hubs are cloud-only for IR.
About local_control: set it to true only if your hub really does emit IR
on local commands. A failed local write is indistinguishable from a good
one — the session authenticates, the write is acknowledged with
retcode=0, and nothing is transmitted. A Vizia Smart IR (category wnykq,
protocol 3.5) behaves exactly like that, while the same commands through
the cloud work fine. Teach is only offered when local_control is on,
since capture depends on the same local path.
To test: set local_control true, restart, and use Teach. If a real press
is captured, your hub supports local control. If capture always times
out, it doesn't — set it back to false and use the cloud transport.
